provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Agriculture: fish and poultry
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list different types of poultry birds.
The pupils should be able to explain basic fish farming needs.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about farm animals. Today we will learn about caring for chickens and fish.
Content:
Poultry birds are chickens, ducks, and guinea fowls. They need clean water and good feed daily. Fish farming is called aquaculture. Fish need clean water, good food and space to swim. Farmers use ponds or tanks to keep fish.
Class activity:
Draw a fish pond and label its parts like water inlet and outlet.
Evaluation questions:
Name two poultry birds.
What do fish need to grow well?
Why is clean water important for chickens?
Summary:
We have learned about caring for chickens and fish in farming.

topics.title: Agriculture: preservation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why we preserve food.
The pupils should be able to list two methods of crop preservation.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about fish and poultry farming. Today we will learn how to preserve crops.
Content:
Preservation means keeping food fresh for a long time. We preserve crops to prevent spoilage and waste. Drying is a common method where we spread crops in the sun. We also store crops in cool dry places. This keeps yams, cassava and maize good to eat for many months.
Class activity:
Show pupils dried fish and explain how the sun removes water to preserve it.
Evaluation questions:
What is preservation?
Name one method of preserving crops.
Why do we preserve our harvest?
Summary:
Preserving food helps us have food all year and reduces waste.

topics.title: Home economics: clothing care
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to wash clothes properly.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to fold a shirt neatly.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about different types of clothes. Today we will learn how to take care of our clothes.
Content:
Washing clothes keeps them clean and fresh. First, sort clothes by color. Then use clean water and soap to wash. After washing, rinse with clean water and dry in the sun. Ironing removes wrinkles and kills germs. Folding clothes neatly keeps them tidy in the wardrobe.
Class activity:
Let pupils practice folding a small cloth neatly and placing it in a box.
Evaluation questions:
What should we do before washing clothes?
Why do we iron our clothes?
How should we store clean clothes?
Summary:
Taking good care of our clothes makes them last longer and look nice.

topics.title: Home economics: simple meals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ingredients for making fruit salad.
The pupils should be able to explain two kitchen safety rules.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about clothing care. Today we will learn to prepare a simple meal and stay safe in the kitchen.
Content:
A fruit salad is a healthy and simple meal. We need fruits like banana, apple, orange and pineapple. We also need a knife, cutting board and bowl. Kitchen safety is very important. Always wash your hands before cooking. Use oven gloves when handling hot pots.
Class activity:
Prepare a simple fruit salad with pupils, teaching them to wash fruits and use knives safely.
Evaluation questions:
Name two fruits for making fruit salad.
Why should we wash our hands before cooking?
What should we use when carrying a hot pot?
Summary:
We can prepare simple meals safely by following good rules in the kitchen.

topics.title: Agriculture: trees and money
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list three cash crops in Nigeria.
The pupils should be able to explain why tree crops are important.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about different crops. Today we will learn about tree crops that bring money to farmers.
Content:
Cash crops are crops that farmers sell to make money. Tree crops include cocoa, palm oil and rubber. Cocoa is used to make chocolate and drinks. Palm oil comes from palm fruit and is used for cooking. These crops bring money to farmers and help our country's economy.
Class activity:
Bring pictures of cocoa and palm trees. Let pupils identify them and name the products we get from them.
Evaluation questions:
Name two cash crops in Nigeria.
What do we use cocoa for?
Why are tree crops important to Nigeria?
Summary:
Tree crops like cocoa and palm oil are important because they bring money to farmers and our country.

topics.title: Home economics: the family budget
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to differentiate between needs and wants.
The pupils should be able to suggest ways to save money.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about cash crops. Today we will learn how families plan their money wisely.
Content:
Needs are things we must have to live, like food, clothes and shelter. Wants are things we like to have but can live without, like toys and sweets. A budget helps families plan their money. We should save money for important things. Putting small change in a piggy bank is a good way to save.
Class activity:
Let pupils make a simple list of things they need and things they want.
Evaluation questions:
What is the difference between needs and wants?
Name one way to save money.
Why should families make a budget?
Summary:
Planning our money helps us buy what we need and save for the future.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship: making crafts
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list materials needed for making bead crafts.
The pupils should be able to suggest a fair price for a simple craft item.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about family budgets. Today we will learn how to make crafts to sell and earn money.
Content:
Craft making is a good business in Nigeria. We can make beautiful things with beads, paper, and thread. Bead crafts are popular and can be sold at the market. When we make crafts to sell, we should think about the price. The price should cover the cost of materials and give us some profit.
Class activity:
Let pupils make simple bead bracelets and practice saying how much they would sell them for.
Evaluation questions:
Name two materials for making crafts.
Why should we think about price when making crafts to sell?
What is profit in craft making?
Summary:
Making crafts is a good way to earn money and learn about business.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship: savings
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of saving money.
The pupils should be able to make a simple savings plan.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about making crafts to sell. Today we will learn how to save the money we earn.
Content:
Saving money means keeping it for future use. A piggy bank is a good place to keep small coins. We should save money for important things like school fees or new books. A savings plan helps us save regularly. For example, we can save 10 naira every day from our pocket money.
Class activity:
Let pupils decorate empty containers to use as piggy banks and write a savings goal on them.
Evaluation questions:
Why is saving money important?
Name one place to keep our savings.
What should we consider when making a savings plan?
Summary:
Saving money helps us prepare for future needs and achieve our goals.

topics.title: Agriculture: farm visit
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different crops on the school farm.
The pupils should be able to record observations about plants.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about cash crops. Today we will visit the school farm to see real plants.
Content:
On the farm, we can see different crops growing. Some plants are tall like maize, others are short like groundnut. We should observe carefully and note what we see. Farmers look at the leaves, stems and fruits to know if the plant is healthy. We can draw what we see in our notebooks.
Class activity:
Take pupils on a walk around the school farm. Let them observe different plants and draw two of them in their notebooks.
Evaluation questions:
What should we look for when observing plants on the farm?
Name two crops you might see on a farm.
Why do farmers check their plants regularly?
Summary:
Visiting a farm helps us learn about plants and how they grow.

topics.title: Revision and exhibition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what they learned this term.
The pupils should be able to display a craft they made.
Introduction:
This term we learned about agriculture, home economics and entrepreneurship. Today we will revise and show what we know.
Content:
We have learned about caring for animals, preserving food, making simple meals, family budget, craft making and saving money. An exhibition is a place to show what we have made. We can display our crafts, drawings and farm records. This helps us share our knowledge with others.
Class activity:
Organize a small exhibition where pupils display their crafts, drawings and farm records.
Evaluation questions:
Name one thing you learned about agriculture this term.
What is a family budget?
Why is saving money important?
Summary:
We have learned many useful skills this term that will help us at home and in the future.
